Collective punishment.

It's been Israeli policy for decades.

In the occupied West Bank, we're witnessing collective punishment in its
purest form after the Israeli military [said](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-
news/israel-security/2026-10-23/ty-article/idf-two-israelis-wounded-in-west-
bank-shooting-attack-near-hebron/000001a1-670e-d29a-a1a5-e7af44bc0000)
suspected Palestinian gunmen killed[ two Israeli soldiers and injured three
others ](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/10/23/five-israelis-
wounded-shooting-hebron-checkpoint-hamas-claims-responsibility/)near a
checkpoint in Hebron on Friday. The suspected assailants were killed in the
attack, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
[ordered](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/10/24/iran-war-live-
israel-launches-targeted-hebron-operation-after-attack) a "full lockdown" of
the occupied West Bank, with Israeli forces conducting raids, [forcibly
displacing Palestinian
families](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/176203), and [demolishing
homes and structures](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/176212) of those
who had nothing to do with the shooting.
